bias.label: Bias
bias.description: A directional tendency in judgment, attention, memory, belief, or choice. The label does not by itself establish how strong, universal, or well-replicated the tendency is.

effect.label: Effect
effect.description: An observed pattern or outcome that appears under particular conditions. An effect name can describe what happens without implying one universal cognitive mechanism.

heuristic.label: Heuristic
heuristic.description: A shortcut or rule of thumb used to make judgments efficiently. A heuristic can be useful in many environments and produce bias when the shortcut is poorly matched to the task.

fallacy.label: Fallacy
fallacy.description: A recurring error in reasoning or argument structure. Fallacies are classified by the logic of the inference rather than by a claim about one psychological mechanism.

phenomenon.label: Phenomenon
phenomenon.description: A broader named pattern, state, or behavioral observation that does not fit cleanly into bias, effect, heuristic, fallacy, or principle.

principle.label: Principle / law
principle.description: A named principle, law, or descriptive regularity. These entries may be useful for understanding cognition without being cognitive biases in the narrow sense.
